# PEN-4357 — backfill the $HOME tooling directories behind the wrapper lead (opencode mirror)

`src/server/job-manifest.ts`, in `buildEnvVars()`: the byte-identical change the
`claude_k8s` adapter takes under the same issue — after `IMAGE_WRAPPER_BIN_DIR`
is made `PATH[0]`, also ensure `<merged.HOME>/.local/bin` and
`<merged.HOME>/bin` are present behind it. See
`vendor/paperclip-adapter-claude-k8s/PROVENANCE-CHANGES.d/pen-4357.md` for the
mechanism, the live measurement and the residual exposure; this entry records
only what differs here.

`src/server/job-manifest.test.ts`: the same five bash-resolution cases and
control, adapted to this file's `mockCtx`/`mockSelfPod` idiom. Three existing
cases in `buildJobManifest — GitHub egress wrapper PATH ordering (PEN-3732)`
are updated: two exact-equality values now carry the backfilled directories,
and "is idempotent when the wrapper directory already leads" is split into a
fixed-point case plus a no-op case. The present-but-late case keeps its original
property — an already-present `/paperclip/.local/bin` is demoted behind the
wrapper — with one added entry in the expected value.

## Latent here, live there — and still worth carrying

As with PEN-3732 itself: there are no `opencode_k8s` workloads, so nothing in
this adapter was resolving `gh`/`git` through the agent-writable PVC copies. The
measurement that motivated this was taken on a pod labelled
`paperclip.io/adapter-type=claude_k8s`. The gap here is structural rather than
observed, and it is carried for the same reason PEN-3732 was: the cost of a
latent gap in a security control is that it goes live silently the first time an
opencode Job is scheduled, and the two adapters are the only K8s execution
targets, so fixing one leaves the other resolving the writable wrappers.

`IMAGE_WRAPPER_BIN_DIR` must stay equal to `paperclip.imageWrapperBinDir` in the
chart and to the identical constant in the `claude_k8s` adapter; this change
does not touch it.
